what: Rung 0's held-out choice accuracy against the majority-class baseline, swept over context width and model capacity. Every point is 3 seeds x 10 epochs over the same file-disjoint split of the same qd-mutate corpus.
why: docs/lappi.md names capacity as 'the first thing to raise if rung 0 underperforms'. The first real rung 0 run underperformed, so this raises it -- along the two axes the doc and the config name -- and measures what each one buys.
host: 192.222.58.240, NVIDIA GH200 480GB, torch 2.10.0+cu128 (the 4096 point is CPU on the Mac)

corpus.split: by source path, hashed, val_share 0.25; 133 train files and 36 val files, 0 on both sides

how_to_read: The baseline is the share of the most common gold class on the validation rows -- the score a model gets by answering that one class every time. Only the GAP between measured and baseline is evidence. A model at the baseline has learned the prior and nothing else.
finding: No configuration beat the majority-class baseline. 15.6x the parameters (1.52M -> 23.8M) and 2x the context moved the held-out number by nothing; the largest models converge ON the baseline rather than above it, which is majority-class collapse -- every held-out row answered with `stub`. Span accuracy stayed at 0.7-1.7% against 0.5% uniform-pointer chance at every point.
what_context_bought: Exactly what the window table predicted for the CORPUS and nothing for the result: 4096 -> 8192 took the usable corpus from 413/161 to 763/303 train/val decisions, and the mean went from -1.4% to +0.0%. The improvement is in the VARIANCE (spread 8.8% -> 0.0%), which is a cleaner reading of the same negative.
honest_caveat: The 512x6 point is plausibly undertrained rather than saturated: its final training loss is ~5.3 against ~1.7 at 256x4 and ~0.97 at 128x2, so 10 epochs / 960 steps does not fit the training set at that size the way it does at the smaller ones. Its held-out number is therefore weaker evidence about capacity than the 128x2 and 256x4 points, which did fit and still did not transfer.
what_this_redirects: Context and capacity are now measured rather than assumed, and neither is the binding constraint. What remains untested is the CORPUS: 763 training decisions drawn from 133 files of one repository, with a gold distribution of stub 51.5% / logic 30.0% / cosmetic 16.7% / clean 1.7%. That is the lever this sweep did not pull.
rule_8: Every row is quick=True and promotes nothing: the corpus is this repository rather than the pool the plan names, which rule 8 counts as a subsample.
